# aeneid-005 — proposed new house renderings

| line | Latin | `l` | `i` |
|---|---|---|---|
| I.462 | *sunt lacrimae rerum et mentem mortalia tangunt* | "are tears of happenings, and the mind the mortal things touch" | "There are tears for what befalls, and the mind is stirred by the lot of mortals." |

I.462 is the set piece listed in `conventions.md` as still undecided; here it is a considered proposal for the owner to confirm. It was built from the Latin alone (`rerum` kept open as the genitive of `res`: events, fortunes; `mortalia` as the neuter plural noun, subject of `tangunt`). The reviewer replaced the drafter's `i` ("Misfortune has its tears, and the mind is stirred by the lot of mortals."), whose first half sat close to the familiar "tears for misfortune" type of rendering, and checked the new wording from memory (no collation) against the well-known published versions: none of "tears of things", "tears for things", "tears at the heart of things", "tears in the nature of things", "tears for misfortune", "touch the heart", "mortal things touch the mind", "mortal sorrows". The reviewer cannot rule out an overlap with some version he does not recall; the owner may wish to confirm.

No other new house renderings: the rest are ordinary renderings of single lines. (I.437 *O fortunati* and I.439 *mirabile dictu* are not house renderings, but both were rephrased away from the stock English; see `review.md`.)
